column3: Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls the servants those of “your lord”; BSB has “my servants.” It specifies a female mule.

The Hebrew says to go up “after him”; BSB has “with him.”

Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “the people” and pairs playing pipes with pipes and rejoicing with joy.
The Hebrew says they had finished eating and separately names Joab as hearing the horn; BSB has “were finishing” and mentions the horn in the first hearing clause.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew refers to the accompanying man as “him”; BSB supplies Solomon.
The Hebrew describes the city becoming stirred and says “you heard”; BSB speaks of rejoicing ringing through it and uses present “hear.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “God” without an explicit “your” and speaks of making the name better; BSB adds “your” and says “more famous.”
The Hebrew explicitly repeats the king as speaker; BSB carries that speaker forward from the preceding verse.
The Hebrew says each went his way; BSB says they “scattered.”
The Hebrew coordinates going and grasping the horns; BSB makes grasping the purpose of going.
The Hebrew repeats “behold” and says the oath is to be made today; BSB has “first.”
The Hebrew calls him a “son of valor”; BSB has “a man of character.”
The Hebrew describes sending, unnamed people bringing him down, and his coming and bowing; BSB condenses these as summoning him down. It repeats Solomon’s name as the final speaker.
